Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
856 AM PST Tue Nov 24 2026

.SYNOPSIS...24/240 AM.

Mild and dry conditions are expected into Tuesday except for some
cold overnight temperatures. Light rain is possible again Tuesday
night into Wednesday morning along the Central coast. Thanksgiving
and Friday will be warm and dry. A cooling trend will begin over 
the weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-THU)...24/855 AM.

***UPDATE***

Offshore flow is increasing again and expecting to see an uptick
in winds this morning in the usual Santa Ana wind favored areas.
Not expecting any advisories today or tomorrow but likely on
Thursday when the ensembles show offshore flow increasing to 
almost -6mb. 

Otherwise, just warming temperatures with some increasing clouds
today through Wednesday morning from a storm moving into northern
California.

***From Previous Discussion***

A decaying cold front will approach the Central Coast Tuesday 
night into Wednesday morning. Short-term high resolution guidance 
continues the trend of less rainfall. Have adjusted POPs and QPF 
amounts to match - 0.05" or less and a 20% chance of a shower 
along the coast. Most areas will see no measurable rain.

Offshore flow with a warming trend will continue through the
work week. Northeasterly winds will peak on Thanksgiving Day 
with potential for low-end wind advisories for favored areas
in the Santa Ana wind corridor such as western San Gabriels 
and Santa Susanna mtns for example. Sub-advisory sundowners
are also likely Wednesday. Temperatures will peak on Black
Friday in the low to mid 80s across the LA basin. 

The biggest concern this week will be at the beaches where
the combination of very high tides and surf will result
in a significant threat for coastal flooding especially
Wednesday and Thursday. Please refer to LAXCFWLOX and
beaches section for more information.

.LONG TERM (FRI-MON)...24/240 AM.

Dry weather will continue through at least Saturday. Temps will 
gradually cool due to ridge breaking down and pressure gradients 
trending strongly onshore. This in response to the approaching 
storm system moving into the Pac NW. The decaying cold front 
associated with aforementioned system will likely produce some 
light rain Sunday into Monday especially along the Central Coast.
Not expecting any hydrological issues (minor at most) at this 
time.

There is a strong signal for another storm right on the heels
of Sunday/Monday's system which looks to tap into Subtropical
moisture. Rough timing of this system would be Tuesday into 
Wednesday. Hydrological issues could be a concern with this 
system as the combined mean of GEFS,EPS, & west-WRF ensemble
forecast is 250 IVT which is borderline Atmospheric River. 
At this time, 1-3 inches in upslope areas looks possible.

&&

.AVIATION...24/1639Z.

At 1630Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer or marine inversion.

For 18Z TAF package, high confidence in VFR for all sites through
the period. There will be a 20-30% chance of showers after 10Z at
KPRB and KSBP, but VFR conditions will prevail.

KLAX...High confidence in 18Z TAF as VFR conditions are expected
through the period. No significant easterly wind component is
expected. 

KBUR...High confidence in 18Z TAF as VFR conditions are expected
through the period.

&&

.MARINE...24/839 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. High confidence in winds and seas remaining below Small
Craft Advisory (SCA) levels through this afternoon. From tonight
through Thursday night, high confidence in combination of Small 
Craft Advisory (SCA) level winds and seas. Seas during this period
will peak between 14 and 18 feet on Wednesday and Wednesday 
night. For Friday through Saturday, high confidence in winds 
remaining below SCA levels, but a 60-80% chance of SCA level seas.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through this afternoon, high 
confidence in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For 
tonight through Thursday night, high confidence in combination of
SCA level winds and seas. Seas during this period will peak 
between 13 and 16 feet on Wednesday. For Friday through Saturday, 
high confidence in winds remaining below SCA levels, but a 40-60% 
chance of SCA level seas. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through tonight, high confidence 
in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For Wednesday, there
is a 50-60% chance of SCA level winds across the western half of 
the Santa Barbara Channel and a 30-40% chance of SCA level seas. 
For Thursday, there is a 50-70% chance of SCA level northeast 
winds from Ventura to Santa Monica and a 40-60% chance of SCA 
level seas. For Friday through Saturday, high confidence in winds 
and seas remaining below SCA levels.

&&

.BEACHES...24/839 AM.

A large, long period, west swell will move into the coastal
waters today and peak on Wednesday and Thursday. This large swell
will combine with very high tides to bring significant surf to 
the area as well as significant coastal flooding.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast as well as the beaches of
Ventura county. Elsewhere, the surf and coastal flooding issues
are a bit less, but still concerning. There will be many, strong
rip currently nearly everywhere, strong long shore currents, a
risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, coastal erosion and
potential for breaking waves in the harbor entrances. 

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
